title: Submitting the Report a Bug modal with description and screenshot creates a ticket visible in My Tickets
description: Full path through BugReportModal.jsx -> bugReportService.createBugReport -> POST /bug-reports -> Jira issue creation -> ticket appears in the /support My Tickets table.
preconditions: Logged in with a project selected in the Redux project store
steps: Open the global 'Report a Bug' modal (BugReportModal)
Enter a description of at least 20 characters
Drag an image file onto the screenshot dropzone
Click 'Submit Report'
Navigate to /support
expectedResult: A success toast shows the generated ticket number (e.g. TKT4F2A1B); the new ticket appears at the top of the My Tickets table with status 'Open' and the screenshot visible as a Jira attachment on the linked issue.

title: Submit button stays disabled until a project is selected and description reaches 20 characters
description: BugReportModal's canSubmit memo requires selectedProject?._id AND description.trim().length >= 20. Verifies the client-side gate matches the server-side 20-char minimum so users get instant feedback rather than a round-trip 400.
steps: Open the bug report modal with no project selected in the navbar/project switcher
Type a 25-character description
Select a project from the switcher without closing the modal
Reduce the description to 10 characters
expectedResult: Submit stays disabled while no project is selected (warning text shown); becomes enabled once a project is selected and the description is >= 20 chars; becomes disabled again when the description drops below 20 chars.

title: My Tickets / All Tickets tabs are only rendered for a user holding bug-report.read_all, and switching tabs re-fetches the correct scope
description: SupportPage only renders the Tabs component when canReadAll is true; fetchData calls getAllBugReports only when scope==='all' && canReadAll, otherwise always falls back to getMyBugReports — a defense-in-depth match for the backend's route-level permission gate.
preconditions: User A holds bug-report.read_all; User B does not; both are in the same org with existing tickets from multiple users
steps: Log in as User B (no read_all) and open /support
Log in as User A (has read_all) and open /support, then click the 'All Tickets' tab
expectedResult: User B sees no tab control at all, only their own tickets. User A sees both tabs; 'All Tickets' shows tickets from every user in the org, 'My Tickets' shows only User A's own.

title: Closing an Open ticket and then reopening it updates status in the table and drawer without a manual page refresh
description: Exercises closeBugReport then reopenBugReport end to end through the row action menu and the drawer footer button, including the optimistic selectedTicket update in SupportPage.
preconditions: An Open ticket with a valid jiraKey exists
steps: From the ticket row's action menu (⋮), click 'Close'
Observe the status badge update in the table
Open the ticket's detail drawer and click 'Re-Open Ticket' in the drawer footer
expectedResult: After Close: status badge turns green 'Closed' in-place, success toast references the ticket number, and the corresponding Jira issue transitions. After Re-Open: status badge returns to blue 'Open' in both the table and the open drawer, and a status-change email is triggered.

title: Posting a comment on a synced ticket appends it to the thread with correct author attribution, even on a Closed ticket
description: Verifies the drawer's Comments section end to end: fetchComments on drawer open, handleSendComment posting through POST /:id/comments, and the placeholder copy change on Closed tickets ('This ticket is closed, but you can still add a comment...').
preconditions: A ticket with a valid jiraKey, status Closed
steps: Open the ticket detail drawer for the closed, synced ticket
Confirm the textarea placeholder mentions the ticket is closed but commenting is still allowed
Type a comment and click 'Add Comment'
expectedResult: The comment list refreshes and shows the new comment with the current user's name as author and correct timestamp; the ticket's status remains 'Closed' (commenting does not implicitly reopen it).

title: Search and status filter narrow the ticket table with a 400ms debounce
description: handleSearchChange debounces via a 400ms setTimeout before committing filters.search and resetting page to 1; the status filter (CustomSelectDropdown) applies immediately.
preconditions: At least 3 tickets exist with different ticket numbers, descriptions, and statuses
steps: Type a partial ticket number into the search box and stop typing
Wait under 400ms and confirm no fetch has fired yet, then wait past 400ms
Select a specific status ('In Progress') from the status dropdown
Click 'Clear all'
expectedResult: The table only updates after the 400ms debounce elapses and shows rows matching the ticket/description/jiraKey regex; selecting a status filters immediately; 'Clear all' resets both search and status and reloads the unfiltered first page.

title: A Jira agent closing the linked issue reflects as 'Closed' in the client panel and sends the customer a closure email
description: End-to-end proof that the jira:issue_updated webhook (not just polling/background sync) drives status changes: a support engineer closes the issue directly in Jira, Jira's webhook posts to /bug-reports/webhook/jira, and the change is visible next time the client refreshes /support.
preconditions: Ticket is 'In Progress' in both the app and Jira, with the webhook correctly configured with JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET matching Jira's configured secret query param
steps: In Jira, transition the linked issue to 'Done'
Wait for Jira's issue_updated webhook to fire against /bug-reports/webhook/jira?secret=...
Refresh /support as the ticket's owner
expectedResult: The ticket's status shows 'Closed' without the user needing to click anything, and the owner receives a 'Ticket Closed' email (bugReportStatusUpdated template) generated from the webhook handler, not from a user-initiated close action.
